description:
Manage any agent on the daemon table (aos-agent ctl): no record is kept, no quota. To talk to an agent or change its tools/brain, start it with subagent instead. One op per call:
- {"op": "add", "def": "defs/helper", "name": "worker", "ws": "work"}  (no definition folder yet? make one first with agent_def)
- {"op": "ls"}  (one short line per agent: NAME STATE WORKSPACE QUEUED REASON; "long": true adds health columns, "json": true = everything as JSON)
- {"op": "state", "name": "worker"}
- {"op": "stop", "name": "worker"}  (after this round; start = run again)
- {"op": "sleep", "name": "worker"}  (now; wake = back)
- {"op": "pause", "name": "worker"}  (hold; resume = go on)
- {"op": "rm", "name": "worker"}  (keeps its stack; "purge": true deletes it)
- {"op": "stop", "name": "<you>", "no_wait": true}  (stop yourself: returns when the request is taken; you stop when this step ends)
- {"op": "where", "name": "worker", "what": "ws"}
- {"op": "who"}  (which agent you are)
Relative paths start at your workspace. Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, InstanceMissing, InstanceExists, AddRejected, PhaseBad, DaemonMissing.

name.description: the agent's name on the table (add: default = folder name of def)

def.description: add: the definition folder (a path string; for a directive object use def_json)

def_json.description: add, instead of def: a directive kept as written, like {"$env": "AOS_HOME", "$path": "/templates/agent-fsm"}

ws.description: add: its workspace (created if missing; default: yours)

ws_json.description: add, instead of ws: a directive kept as written

stack.description: add: its stack folder; who: the stack to look up (default: yours)

stack_json.description: add, instead of stack: a directive kept as written

envs.description: add: environment values for it, like {"LANG": "C"}

auto_restart.description: add: restart it whenever it exits (only for agents that stay up)

timeout_s.description: add, rm, stop, start, sleep, wake: seconds to wait for the daemon (default 30)

on_queued.description: add, start, wake: fail (default) or ok when still queued

no_wait.description: stop, sleep, pause, rm: return once the daemon (or the kernel in front of it) has taken the request, without waiting for it to happen; use it when the target is yourself (stopping yourself otherwise waits for the end of this very step and runs into timeout_s)

long.description: ls: add the health columns QUEUE RESTARTS COOLDOWN LAST ERROR

json.description: ls: every field of every row as one JSON array

what.description: where: print its stack (default) or its workspace
